hero.title: Start from the right workspace before you draw the first table.
hero.description: Smart ERD is organized around team context, project hubs, document hubs, and a shared dictionary. This page explains the real product flow without going into editor-level DSL syntax.
hero.snapshotDescription: Move through the same structure the app already uses today instead of guessing where each task lives.

product.title: The product is a workspace flow, not a single canvas.
product.description: Teams hold shared operating context, projects bundle planning views, and document hubs hold the actual working files.

teamShared.title: Team-scoped context
teamShared.description: Members, roles, and the shared dictionary live at the team level so multiple projects can reuse the same standards.

projectFocused.title: Project hub first
projectFocused.description: Each project has a hub for documents and adjacent planning views instead of sending you directly into an editor.

documentDriven.title: Document-driven execution
documentDriven.description: ERD, Markdown, and Screen Spec documents are created from the document hub, then opened in the editor route that fits each type.

quickStart.title: Quick start without guesswork.
quickStart.description: Follow this order when you are new to the product or when you need to explain the standard flow to someone else.

step1.title: Log in or create your account
step1.description: Use the public auth screens first. The guide stays public so you can review the product flow before signing in.

step2.title: Choose or create a team
step2.description: The team is the top-level workspace. Shared members and dictionary assets are managed from there.

step3.title: Open the project hub
step3.description: Move from Teams to Projects, then choose the project that owns the current document and planning work. From there you will use WBS, Gantt, My Tasks, and issues from the same hub.

step4.title: Create the right document
step4.description: Start from the document hub. Markdown documents can be linked back into WBS work as reusable context, and ERD work should attach the correct dictionary context.

workspaceMap.title: Use this mental model when deciding where work belongs.
workspaceMap.description: The same task often feels clearer once you know whether it belongs in the team layer, the project layer, or a specific document.

team.title: Teams
team.description: Manage shared membership and enter the team-owned project list from here.

project.title: Projects
project.description: Choose the project that needs execution work, then open its hub. Documents, WBS, Gantt, and My Tasks move together inside that project.

documentHub.title: Document hub
documentHub.description: Create or open ERD, Markdown, and Screen Spec documents in one place. Those documents can later be linked from WBS items or personal TODOs.

dictionary.title: Dictionary
dictionary.description: Maintain reusable words, terms, and domains that ERD work can reference consistently.

projectHub.title: These are the actual project-hub tabs available today.
projectHub.description: The project route is more than a document list. Use the surrounding tabs for planning, tracking, coordination, and personal TODO management.

overview.title: Business Overview
overview.description: Capture the project's core context and align the next execution window.

wbs.title: WBS
wbs.description: Break work into structure and manage the work tree directly in the hub. Each item can carry linked documents, comments, and activity history.

gantt.title: Gantt
gantt.description: Review schedule and milestone progress on a shared timeline. TODOs linked to WBS can be checked here as shared schedule risk context.

myTasks.title: My Tasks
myTasks.description: Manage personal TODOs in a private workspace and only promote them into shared project context when you link them to WBS.

staffing.title: Staffing
staffing.description: Track planned versus actual staffing and labor cost for the project.

issues.title: Issues
issues.description: Register and filter project issues, then export the current list when needed.

documentHub.title: Document hub is where creation starts.
documentHub.description: Create the working document first, then move into the corresponding editor route. Created documents can later be referenced from WBS items or personal TODOs.

erd.title: ERD document
erd.description: Start an ERD canvas with dictionary context attached so tables, relations, and sync flows are ready from the first screen.

markdown.title: Markdown document
markdown.description: Use Markdown for notes, plans, and structured text documents alongside ERD work in the same project. Add tags so the Tags tab can find them again, then link them into WBS items or personal TODOs.

screenSpec.title: Screen Spec document
screenSpec.description: Screen Spec exists as a collaborative screen-design document. Treat it as a supported document type, not a promise that every downstream workflow is already complete.

dictionary.title: Dictionary is shared infrastructure for consistent naming.
dictionary.description: Keep reusable naming assets in one place so ERD work can attach the right context instead of redefining terms per document.

sets.title: Dictionary sets
sets.description: Create and choose dictionary sets that documents can attach to.

assets.title: Words, terms, and domains
assets.description: Each asset type has a different job in naming and standardization, so keep them in the shared dictionary instead of scattering them across documents.

binding.title: Document binding
binding.description: ERD documents reference dictionary context from the hub, while the dictionary itself stays a team-shared workspace.

confusions.title: Common points that confuse first-time users.
confusions.description: These are the boundary lines that are easiest to miss when you enter the product for the first time.

flow.title: Why doesn't this page explain every editor action?
flow.description: Because /guide is the top-level map. It explains product flow such as WBS document links, comments and activity, and My Tasks boundaries, while detailed editor syntax and error examples stay closer to the editor.

projectVsDocument.title: Project vs document
projectVsDocument.description: A project holds multiple planning surfaces and documents. The actual ERD or Markdown file is created in the project's document hub, and WBS uses links to those documents instead of storing long-form content itself.

dictionaryContext.title: Dictionary vs dictionary context
dictionaryContext.description: The dictionary workspace manages shared assets. A dictionary context is the specific set an ERD document attaches when it needs those assets.

todoPrivacy.title: When does My Tasks become shared?
todoPrivacy.description: My Tasks stays private by default. Only TODOs linked to WBS appear in shared project context for schedule and risk tracking.

dsl.title: Where is the detailed DSL syntax guide?
dsl.description: The detailed ERD DSL syntax and diagnostic guides remain in the editor. Use this page for product flow, then switch to the in-editor guide when writing or fixing DSL.

detailCallout.title: Use this page to orient yourself, then switch to the workspace that matches the job.
detailCallout.description: If you need detailed ERD DSL syntax, examples, or error-handling steps, move into the editor workflow. This public guide intentionally stays at the product-flow level.

syntaxGuide.title: Logical DSL Syntax Guide
syntaxGuide.description: DSL is written in Table blocks. Missing or mismatched braces are treated as syntax errors.
syntaxGuide.structureRule1: A table must be declared as '{{tableKeyword}} logicalTableName' with a brace block.
syntaxGuide.structureRule2: Write one column per line inside the block.
syntaxGuide.columnRule1: Use options in brackets: '{{pk}}' primary key, '{{ai}}' auto increment, '{{nn}}' NOT NULL.
syntaxGuide.invalidRule1: 'Table User' without a block is invalid. Always write '{' and '}' together.
syntaxGuide.invalidRule2: Unclosed blocks or standalone '{' are marked as syntax errors.
syntaxGuide.invalidRule3: Using ':Domain' and '::Type' together on the same column is invalid.

errorGuide.title: DSL Error Explanation & Fix Guide
errorGuide.description: Select a diagnostic to see the cause and recommended fixes step by step.
errorGuide.emptyNoIssues: No diagnostics for the current filter.
errorGuide.emptyNoInput: Enter DSL code to see diagnostic guidance.
errorGuide.selectHint: Select a diagnostic item from the left list.

quickAction.keyboardHint: Press Enter to run · Esc to close

syntaxError.cause: The parser could not read the line because the DSL syntax format (table block, column expression, braces/symbols) is invalid.
syntaxError.action1: Check if table declaration follows 'Table TableName {' and has a closing '}'.
syntaxError.action2: Check each column line matches one of: 'LogicalName', 'LogicalName :Domain', 'LogicalName > Table.Column', '[PK, AI, NN]'.
syntaxError.action3: Remove typos/unnecessary symbols, then re-check line by line.
syntaxError.rule: In strict mode, a Table declaration must always include both '{' and '}'.

unknownTerm.cause: The logical name is not registered in the term dictionary, so physical name/domain cannot be resolved.
unknownTerm.action1: Register the term first in the data dictionary.
unknownTerm.action2: If it already exists, verify spelling, spaces, and casing.
unknownTerm.action3: For quick progress, replace it with an already registered logical term.
unknownTerm.rule: DSL logical names should match dictionary terms for stable physical/domain mapping.

unknownDomain.cause: The domain logical name specified on the column does not exist in the dictionary.
unknownDomain.action1: Check whether the domain exists in the domain dictionary.
unknownDomain.action2: Fix the domain name to an existing exact logical name.
unknownDomain.action3: If missing, create the domain first and parse again.
unknownDomain.rule: ':DomainName' only accepts domain logical names that exist in the dictionary.

unknownFkTable.cause: The parent table in the FK expression is not declared in the current DSL document.
unknownFkTable.action1: Declare the referenced table in the DSL first.
unknownFkTable.action2: Verify the parent table logical name spelling.
unknownFkTable.action3: If FK is not needed, remove '>' and keep it as a regular column.
unknownFkTable.rule: FK parent tables must be declared in the same DSL document.

unknownFkColumn.cause: The referenced parent table exists, but the referenced parent column is not declared in that table.
unknownFkColumn.action1: Check whether the target column exists in the parent table block.
unknownFkColumn.action2: Fix typo in the referenced column logical name.
unknownFkColumn.action3: Add the missing column to parent table if needed, then parse again.
unknownFkColumn.rule: FK requires both 'ParentTable.ParentColumn' to exactly match declared names.

domainAndTypeConflict.cause: The same column line declares both a domain (:DomainName) and an explicit type (::TYPE).
domainAndTypeConflict.action1: If you want domain-based typing, remove '::TYPE'.
domainAndTypeConflict.action2: If you want explicit typing, remove ':DomainName'.
domainAndTypeConflict.rule: A single column can use either ':domain' or '::type', not both.

invalidTypeFormat.cause: The type string after '::' does not match the accepted format.
invalidTypeFormat.action1: Use an identifier-based SQL type form, e.g. VARCHAR(200), BIGINT.
invalidTypeFormat.action2: Remove invalid symbols or malformed parentheses and retry.
invalidTypeFormat.rule: Explicit type mapping must follow '::TYPE' format, typically SQL type notation.

noDomainWarning.cause: No domain is linked to this term, so a default physical type is used.
noDomainWarning.action1: Link a domain to the term in dictionary to keep type consistency.
noDomainWarning.action2: Or explicitly assign ':DomainName' in DSL for deterministic type mapping.
noDomainWarning.rule: Warnings do not block apply, but resolving them improves schema quality.

duplicateColumnLogicalNameError.cause: The same column logical name is declared more than once in a single table block.
duplicateColumnLogicalNameError.action1: Rename one of the duplicated column logical names so each column is unique in the table.
duplicateColumnLogicalNameError.action2: If unintentional, remove or merge the duplicated line.
duplicateColumnLogicalNameError.rule: Column logical names must be unique within the same table.

duplicateColumnPhysicalNameError.cause: Duplicate physical column names exist in the same table, which will fail at DB schema level.
duplicateColumnPhysicalNameError.action1: Change one column's term/logical name or update mapped dictionary physical name to remove collision.
duplicateColumnPhysicalNameError.action2: If accidental, remove or merge the duplicated column line.
duplicateColumnPhysicalNameError.rule: Physical column names must be unique within a table.

genericError.action1: Reduce surrounding syntax to isolate the smallest failing fragment.
genericError.action2: Compare with syntax guide examples and fix differences.
genericError.rule: When unsure, narrow down input and validate incrementally.

genericWarning.cause: This is a recommended check warning.
genericWarning.action1: You may proceed first and clean up later if not blocking.
genericWarning.action2: Align dictionary/reference rules when possible to remove warnings.
genericWarning.rule: Fewer warnings generally improve team-level DSL quality and reuse.
